transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. Um, I'm here because... well, things at the lab have been a little... scattered lately. I'm a physical scientist, and usually I'm very on top of things, I promise. But recently, I just can't seem to keep my mind on the actual experiments I'm supposed to be running. 

Like, I'll be in the middle of a really important grant call or a safety meeting, and I'll just... notice things. A slight vibration in one of the vacuum pumps, or a student whispering something in the hallway, or I'll remember some odd peak in a spectrum from three years ago. And suddenly, I'm just off chasing that down for hours. It's not that I don't care about the main project, it's just my brain gets so pulled away. And then the things everyone actually needs from me kind of... fall apart. Is that something you can help with? I really want to get back to being a good team member.
How much distress or anxiety do these distractions cause you?

Oh, um... honestly? It doesn't really cause me anxiety when it happens. I hope that doesn't make me sound, you know, careless or irresponsible. In the moment, it actually feels... fine? My mind just feels really engaged with whatever new detail I've noticed, so it doesn't feel distressing at all. 

I guess the only thing that makes me feel a little bad is just... knowing I might be inconveniencing my colleagues later. I really hate being a burden to the team. But the distractions themselves, the actual pulling away of my attention? No, I wouldn't say that makes me anxious. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining this right.
Do you feel like you have any control over when your mind starts to focus on these details or distractions?

Oh, um... I try really hard to stay on track, I promise I do. But as for actual control over when it starts... I'm not entirely sure? I guess I haven't really thought about it that way. It just sort of happens before I even realize I've shifted gears. 

I hope that's an okay answer. I really don't want to sound like I'm just letting myself get distracted on purpose, because I honestly do try to be disciplined for the team. I just haven't really noticed a specific moment where I choose to focus on the new thing, if that makes sense? Is it normal to not really know if you have control over it? I can definitely try to pay more attention to that next time, if it would be helpful for you!
Do you feel like you have to investigate or resolve the distractions that catch your attention, or can you simply let them go?

Oh, um... I don't know if I feel like I *have* to resolve them? I hope that's an okay answer. It's not like a... a forced feeling, I don't think. I just sort of find myself looking into whatever caught my eye before I even try to let it go. 

I really don't want to sound like I'm just doing whatever I want instead of my actual job, I promise. It's just that I get so interested in the new detail that I don't even think to stop myself and try to ignore it. I guess I haven't really tested if I can just let it go? 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably not a very helpful answer. I should probably be trying harder to just drop those thoughts, shouldn't I? I can definitely try to practice letting things go this week if you think that would be a good idea!
Do you find yourself repeating certain actions or rituals in your daily life?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I have my regular morning routine for getting to the lab and setting up my equipment, but... not like rituals or anything I feel like I *have* to repeat over and over. 

I hope I'm understanding your question right? I just try to keep a pretty normal schedule so I can be reliable for my team. Is it okay if I don't really have anything like that to report? I promise I would tell you if I did. I really want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information so I'm not wasting your time.
Do you ever find yourself becoming extremely focused on a task or activity for an extended period of time?

Oh, um... well, I do work in a lab, so being focused on an experiment for a while is sort of part of the job description. But... I don't think I get *extremely* focused in a way that's bad or anything? 

I mean, I definitely try to be thorough and do good work for my team. Sometimes I'll get really into analyzing a data set and the afternoon just sort of flies by, but I think that's pretty normal for a scientist, right? I hope that doesn't sound like I'm doing something wrong. I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job. Is it okay that I get absorbed in my work sometimes? I can try to take more breaks if you think I should be doing that instead!
Do you feel like the details that distract you are important because they might affect the outcome or quality of your work?

Oh, um... I mean, I definitely want to make sure I'm doing things right at the lab. Quality is really important in our field. But... I don't know if I'd say the distractions are always about the outcome of the work? 

Sometimes a detail just seems really interesting in the moment, even if it's not strictly related to the main experiment. I hope that doesn't make me sound unprofessional. I really do try to focus on what matters most for the team. 

I guess... maybe I just get a little overly curious sometimes? Is that a bad thing? I can definitely try to be more disciplined about only focusing on things that directly affect the results, if you think that would be better. I just want to make sure I'm being a good scientist.
Do you often feel guilty or self-critical when you realize you've been distracted from your main tasks?

Oh, um... well, maybe a little bit? I mean, I think anyone would feel a little bad if they got sidetracked and fell behind, right? 

But I wouldn't say I get, like, *extremely* guilty or beat myself up over it or anything. I just try to quickly course-correct and get back to what I'm supposed to be doing. I really try to be responsible and not let my team down. 

I hope it's normal to feel a little twinge of guilt when you get distracted? I just want to make sure I'm doing my fair share and not causing problems for anyone else. If you think I'm being too hard on myself, I can definitely try to work on that! I really value your opinion on this.
Do you ever find yourself having thoughts that repeatedly come back to you, even when you try to focus on something else?

Oh, um... not really? I mean, I think my mind is pretty clear most of the time. 

Sometimes if I have a big presentation coming up or, you know, a deadline for a grant proposal, I might think about it a lot, just to make sure I'm prepared. But I don't think I have thoughts that just get stuck or keep bothering me when I'm trying to do other things. I can usually just put things out of my mind if I need to focus on my work.

I hope that's the right answer? I just try to stay positive and focused on the present. Is it normal to not really have repetitive thoughts like that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need.
Do you feel like there's something driving you to explore these details, even if you're not sure why they're important?

Oh, um... I wouldn't say there's like, a *drive*, necessarily? That makes it sound a bit... intense, maybe? 

I think it's more just... a natural curiosity, you know? Like, as a scientist, you're trained to observe things, so if something catches my eye, I might just follow it for a minute. It's not like I feel compelled or forced to do it. It's just a quick little detour, and then I get right back to the main task. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound easily distracted or anything. I promise I get my work done! I just like to be thorough. Is that okay? I mean, do you think it's alright to just be a little curious sometimes, as long as it doesn't get in the way?
Do you feel like you need to understand or resolve the details that distract you in order to feel like you've done your work correctly?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I *need* to resolve them. I mean, I definitely don't get stuck on things like that. 

I think I just like to be thorough, you know? Like, if I'm looking at some data and I notice a little anomaly, I might just peek at it for a second to make sure it's not going to mess up the whole experiment. But I can easily just let it go if it's not relevant. I definitely don't feel like I have to figure out every little thing to do my job right. I know how to prioritize.

I really try to be efficient and focus on the big picture. I hope that's the kind of approach you'd expect from someone in my position? I just want to make sure I'm doing things the right way.
Do you think you'd be satisfied with your work if you didn't explore every detail that catches your attention?

Oh, absolutely! Yes, um... I'd definitely still be satisfied. 

I mean, in science, you kind of have to know when to draw the line, right? If you chased down every single tiny detail, you'd never finish a project or get a grant submitted. So I'm actually very comfortable just... letting the little things go if they aren't part of the main objective. I definitely don't need to look into everything to feel like I did a good job. 

I really try to be practical about it and just trust my training. I hope that sounds like a healthy way to handle it? I just want to make sure I'm functioning the way I'm supposed to, and that I'm giving you the right impression of how I work.
Do you feel like you're trying to perfect something when you get distracted by these details?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say that at all. I definitely don't think of myself as a perfectionist. 

I mean, I want my work to be accurate, of course, because of the field I'm in... but I'm not trying to make everything flawless. I feel like perfectionism can really, you know, slow a person down, and I always try to be a good team player and keep my projects moving forward. I'm really careful not to get obsessive about things like that. 

Does that make sense? I just really wouldn't want you to think I'm stuck on trying to be perfect or that I can't let things go. I try to keep a pretty healthy balance with my work... I hope that's what you're looking for?
Do you think you'd get distracted by these details if you felt completely confident that your work was correct?

Oh, um... I think so? I mean, I feel pretty confident in my work most of the time. 

Even when I know I've done everything right, sometimes a little detail just catches my eye, you know? It's not because I'm doubting myself or my results. It's more like... just a natural curiosity, I guess. I definitely don't get distracted because I'm insecure about my work. I have a lot of experience in my field.

I just want to be sure I'm doing things the way a good scientist should. It's normal to be a little curious sometimes, right? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I don't trust my own abilities. I really do try to be confident in what I produce.
Do you think you might be using these distractions as a way to avoid doing certain tasks or dealing with specific emotions?

Oh, goodness, no. Um... I really don't think so. I mean, I've always been a very dedicated worker, so if a task needs to get done, I just roll up my sleeves and do it. I definitely wouldn't use little details as an excuse to procrastinate or... or hide from my feelings, or anything like that. 

I try to be really proactive about my responsibilities. I just handle things head-on, you know? I'm actually pretty good at managing my workload, I promise. I really hope it doesn't seem like I'm trying to run away from the hard parts of my job, or my life. I really do try my best to stay on top of everything and be reliable... is that the kind of approach you'd expect someone to have? I just want to make sure I'm handling things the right way.
Do you feel like exploring these details helps you feel more in control of your work or environment?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say it's about control. I really don't feel like I have any control issues or anything like that. 

I mean, I'm very comfortable working in a team and letting other people take the lead. I don't need to micromanage my environment to feel secure, you know? I'm actually pretty adaptable. When a detail catches my attention, it's just... well, just me being thorough, I think. Not me trying to dominate the project or clinging to control. 

I really try to be easygoing and flexible at work. I know how difficult it can be to work with someone who needs to control everything, and I definitely don't want to be that kind of person. I hope it doesn't come across like I'm trying to control everything around me? I just really value being cooperative and easy to work with.
Do you think your distractions are related to making sure everything is just right in your work?

Oh, um... well, maybe a little bit? But definitely not in a bad way, I promise. I don't think I'm, like, a perfectionist or anything extreme like that. 

I mean, as a scientist, you do want to make sure your data is accurate, right? So if I get a little sidetracked double-checking a measurement or looking into a small anomaly, it's just because I want to do a good job. I really don't obsess over making things flawless. I know good enough is usually just fine, and I'm very capable of moving on when a task is finished. 

I just want to be a diligent worker, you know? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm too rigid or difficult to please. I really do try to just do my best and be satisfied with that... is that the right way to look at it?
Do you think your distractions might be a way for your mind to temporarily escape from feelings of anxiety or stress related to your work?

Oh, goodness, no. Um... I really don't think so. I mean, I don't feel like I'm overly anxious or stressed about my work, honestly. 

I know my job can be demanding sometimes, but I actually feel like I handle stress pretty well. I don't feel the need to escape or hide from it. If things get busy, I just take a deep breath and keep going. I definitely wouldn't want you to think I'm overwhelmed or that I can't handle the pressure of my position. I really do try to stay calm and grounded. 

I mean, everyone has a busy day now and then, right? But I don't use distractions to run away from that. I just try to keep a positive attitude and get through it. I hope that sounds like a healthy way to manage things? I just really want to make sure I'm dealing with work the right way.
Are these distractions affecting your relationships with colleagues, friends, or family outside of work?

Oh, um... no, I really don't think so. I mean, I try very hard to be a good colleague and a supportive friend. I certainly wouldn't want my work habits to bother anyone else.

I think I get along quite well with everyone at the lab, and I always make sure to be present when I'm with my family. If I get a little sidetracked during a conversation, it's just a momentary lapse, you know? It's not because I don't care about what they're saying. I always try to apologize right away if I drift off for a second. 

I really value my relationships and I wouldn't let anything jeopardize them. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm neglecting the people in my life? I just try my best to be there for everyone and be a good listener. I think I do an okay job of balancing everything... at least, I hope I do?
Are you finding that these distractions are affecting your ability to complete tasks or activities outside of your job?

Oh, um... outside of my job? Well, at home, I think I manage okay. But, um... I guess I should mention, since you're asking about completing tasks... things at the lab have gotten a little... complicated lately. 

I really didn't want to bring this up because it makes me sound so incapable, and I promise I'm usually very on top of things. But, um... my department actually had to step in recently on some decisions I usually handle. I guess I missed a few priorities and got some scheduling confused. And... well, they said my supervision was strained and it was putting the project and, um, lab safety expectations at risk. 

It sounds so much worse than it is, I swear! I just had a lot on my plate, and maybe I got a little too distracted. I'm working so hard to fix it and show them I can still do my job perfectly well. I really hope you don't think less of me for that... everyone makes mistakes sometimes, right? I'm just trying to be honest so we can figure this out... is it okay that I told you that?
